summary: Legacy CGI pricing engine with HTML-only output, no authentication, no observability, and critical security vulnerabilities. Cannot be safely integrated with AI agents.

findings.description: No machine-readable API — endpoint returns only HTML (text/html). No JSON, XML, or structured response format.
No API specification or schema (no OpenAPI, WSDL, or contract). Agents cannot discover or validate the interface.
No error codes or structured error responses. All requests return HTTP 200 regardless of input validity.
No input validation — negative quantities accepted, no feedback on malformed input.
Simple 2-parameter interface (sku, qty) would be straightforward to wrap in a structured API.
No authentication mechanism. Endpoint configured with 'Require all granted' — completely open.
No authorization or access control. No roles, scopes, or permissions concept.
No request attribution or caller identification. Audit of agent activity is impossible.
Network-level isolation via K8s ClusterIP is not a substitute for application-level identity.
Endpoint is inherently idempotent — read-only price lookup with no side effects.
Pricing rules in flat file with no versioning, no transactional guarantees, edited in-place on prod.
No caching headers or ETags — agents cannot detect pricing data changes.
Stateless CGI process — no persistent state modified by the endpoint.
No human-in-the-loop controls — no approval workflows, confirmation steps, or escalation paths.
No rate limiting or circuit breakers. Autonomous agents can issue unlimited requests.
Read-only endpoint reduces HITL urgency, but lack of guardrails allows unrestricted pricing data enumeration.
No CI/CD pipeline or deployment approval gates — manual kubectl apply with no review.
No application-level logging. CGI binary produces zero log output.
No metrics endpoint (no Prometheus, CloudWatch, or StatsD). Cannot monitor agent behavior.
No distributed tracing or correlation IDs. Agent requests cannot be traced.
Apache access/error logs exist but are unstructured and not exported to centralized systems.
K8s readiness/liveness probes provide basic availability signaling only.
Buffer overflow — strcpy() with attacker-controlled input into fixed-size stack buffers. Remote code execution possible.
Reflected XSS — SKU parameter printed directly into HTML without escaping.

remediationPriorities: Fix critical security vulnerabilities (buffer overflow, XSS)
Add machine-readable API (JSON responses, proper HTTP status codes)
Implement authentication (API key, OAuth2, or mTLS)
Add rate limiting per authenticated caller
